published_statement: Penrose 1979, verbatim (page images). Gravitational clumping, p.612: 'This is essentially an effect of the universally attractive nature of the gravitational interaction. As a gravitating system "relaxes" more and more, velocities increase and the sources clump together -- instead of uniformly spreading throughout space in a more familiar high-entropy arrangement. ... In the absence of significant non-gravitational forces, when dissipative effects come further into play, clumping becomes more and more marked as the entropy increases. Finally, maximum entropy is achieved with collapse to a black hole'. Weyl and clumping, p.614: 'In terms of spacetime curvature, the absence of clumping corresponds, very roughly, to the absence of Weyl conformal curvature (since absence of clumping implies spatial-isotropy, and hence no gravitational principal null-directions). When clumping takes place, each clump is surrounded by a region of nonzero Weyl curvature. As the clumping gets more pronounced owing to gravitational contraction, new regions of empty space appear with Weyl curvature of greatly increased magnitude.' No measure, p.615: 'The indications are, then, that a high-entropy singularity should involve a very large Weyl curvature, unlike the situation of the singularity in the Friedmann dust-filled universe or any other models of the Robertson-Walker class. At the time of writing, however, no clear-cut integral formula (say) which could be regarded as giving mathematical expression to this suggested relation between Weyl curvature and gravitational entropy has come to light.' The hypothesis, p.630: 'I propose, then, that there should be a complete lack of chaos in the initial geometry. ... So the "lowness" of the initial entropy was not a result of some special matter distribution, but, instead, of some very special initial spacetime geometry. The indications of sections 12.2.6 and 12.3.1, in particular, are that this restriction on the early geometry should be something like: the Weyl curvature C_abcd vanishes at any initial singularity.' with footnote 'That is, with the notation of section 12.3.2, at d^-M. Note that this includes the final singular TIF of a Hawking black hole explosion -- at which the Weyl curvature indeed vanishes!'; and 'This hypothesis is still a little vague, and is open to a number of different interpretations.' p.631: 'My inclination is to try, first, the simplest of these, namely that C_abcd -> 0 (in, say, any parallelly propagated frame), as initial singularities are approached.' Status, p.632: 'I am hypothesizing, here, that there are in fact (local) physical laws which only become important near spacetime singularities, these being asymmetric in time and such as to force the Weyl curvature to vanish at any initial singular point'. Consequence, p.634: 'With the Weyl curvature initially zero and thermal equilibrium for the matter (and radiation), we shall have something very close to spatial-isotropy and homogeneity for the initial state.' and 'White holes are excluded at all times, because their singularities are "initial" singularities (i.e. points of d^-M) which do not remotely satisfy the constraint C_abcd = 0.' Section title, p.629: '12.3.3 A hypothesis and a world-view'.
published_hypotheses: READ (p.630-632): a proposed, time-asymmetric LOCAL LAW acting at INITIAL singularities ('I am hypothesizing ... (local) physical laws which only become important near spacetime singularities, these being asymmetric in time'). It is not a theorem of GR. The source calls it 'a hypothesis' (section 12.3.3 title) and 'still a little vague'.

READ (p.630-631): the condition is at 'any initial singularity' (d^-M), in one of several versions (C -> 0; a faster rate; bounded; Ricci-dominated). Penrose chooses 'C_abcd -> 0 (in, say, any parallelly propagated frame)'. The time asymmetry comes from the initial/final distinction; white-hole singularities count as initial and are excluded (p.634).
READ (p.615): the Weyl-entropy relation is 'suggested'. There is 'no clear-cut integral formula', so there is no measure of gravitational entropy.
READ (p.612): clumping raises entropy 'In the absence of significant non-gravitational forces, when dissipative effects come further into play'; the maximum is 'collapse to a black hole'.
READ (p.614): absence of clumping corresponds to absence of Weyl curvature only 'very roughly'.

READ (p.634): the consequence drawn for the early universe, 'something very close to spatial-isotropy and homogeneity for the initial state', with fluctuations that 'must occur -- because the initial restrictions on R_ab are statistical, unlike those on C_abcd'.
hypothesis_drift: STATUS DROPPED (confirmed by reading): permute.py:88-89 names it 'Penrose's hypothesis', which matches the source's own word (p.629 section title, p.630 'This hypothesis is still a little vague'). But permute.py:441-443 prints 'Penrose: the early universe had near-zero Weyl curvature, so gravitational clumping IS a relaxation', and permute.py:543-545 prints 'But the early universe had near-zero Weyl curvature and gravitational clumping raises entropy'. Both state as fact what the source proposes as a conjectural, time-asymmetric law, one whose link to entropy is 'suggested' with 'no clear-cut integral formula' (p.615).

CONDITION DROPPED (new, from reading): the source's clumping-entropy statement carries 'In the absence of significant non-gravitational forces, when dissipative effects come further into play' (p.612). permute.py:89-90 and 544 ('gravitational clumping raises it' / 'raises entropy') state it without that condition.

WITHDRAWN (first audit's 'ADDED: relaxation is the tree's own term and does not come from the source'): the source uses it. p.612: 'As a gravitating system "relaxes" more and more, velocities increase and the sources clump together' and '... as the system relaxes'. The owner's 'Structure formation is genuinely a relaxation' (permute.py:90) follows Penrose's usage. Penrose puts it in scare quotes the first time; the owner does not.

WITHDRAWN as a drift (first audit's SCOPE item, deferred until read): the owner's 'the early universe' against the source's 'initial singularity'. Penrose himself draws the consequence for the initial state: p.634 'we shall have something very close to spatial-isotropy and homogeneity for the initial state', and FLRW is conformally flat (first audit C1). The owner's 'Weyl curvature near zero' in the early universe is the source's own inference, not a widening of it.

The first audit's C2 point (C_abcd C^abcd is time-symmetric and carries no arrow by itself) agrees with the source, which gets the arrow from the initial/final distinction (p.630 'at any initial singularity'; p.634 white holes excluded).

data_at_publication.quantity: Baryon number and entropy per baryon (Penrose's own inputs)
data_at_publication.value_then: READ p.629: 'Consider a closed recollapsing universe containing, say, 10^80 baryons'; 'an entropy per baryon of ~10^9' (p.629, the photon-to-baryon figure). READ p.630: M_sun black hole 'an entropy per baryon of 10^18'; '10^10 M_sun galaxy with a 10^6 M_sun black hole core has an entropy per baryon of 10^20'; whole galaxy in the hole '10^28'; 'an immense final entropy per baryon of ~10^40'; 'the absurdly small fraction of at most ~10^-31 of the "available chaos"'.
data_at_publication.value_now: Computed from the Bekenstein-Hawking formula Penrose prints on p.602 (S = k A c^3/4 hbar G, i.e. S/k = 4 pi G M^2/hbar c): 8.83e19, 8.83e21, 8.83e29 and 7.42e42 per baryon. The three galactic figures are each low by the same factor, 88 (1.95 dex). The final figure is low by 742 (2.87 dex). 10^9/10^40 = 10^-31 is internally consistent.
data_at_publication.source_now: reaudit P1-P2; CODATA-class constants in the script (G, hbar, c, M_sun, m_p)
data_at_publication.moves_conclusion: No. The owner uses no number from Penrose. With the printed figures the gap from radiation entropy to the maximal entropy is 31 dex; with the formula it is 33.9 dex (reaudit P5). 'Extremely low' survives either way. The printed figures are order-of-magnitude underestimates of the source's own formula. That is recorded as a finding about the source's arithmetic, not repaired, and it is not an error of the owner.

lacked_data: READ: in 1979 Penrose had CMB uniformity 'to one part in ~10^3' and a rotation bound '<10^-16 s^-1' (p.634). He had no measure of gravitational entropy, and said so (p.615). The gap that matters is conceptual, not observational. Later data cannot supply a definition, and the data-dependent part (the >30 dex entropy gap) does not move: 31 dex on his printed figures, 33.9 dex on his own formula. M's hypothesis is not supported for this result.

grade_evidence: READ, Penrose 1979 p.630: 'this restriction on the early geometry should be something like: the Weyl curvature C_abcd vanishes at any initial singularity ... This hypothesis is still a little vague'. p.615: 'no clear-cut integral formula ... giving mathematical expression to this suggested relation between Weyl curvature and gravitational entropy has come to light'. p.632: 'I am hypothesizing ... (local) physical laws ... asymmetric in time'. p.612: 'As a gravitating system "relaxes" more and more ... In the absence of significant non-gravitational forces, when dissipative effects come further into play, clumping becomes more and more marked as the entropy increases.' permute.py:87-91 renders this correctly and labels it 'Penrose's hypothesis'. Even 'relaxation' is the source's word. But the verdict lines permute.py:441-443 and 543-545 state the hypothesis as established fact and drop the p.612 condition. The scorecard's 'the REARRANGEMENT relaxes' (permute.py:507-508) rests on a literal compared with itself (permute.py:273, 439-440). So the tree uses the result without the hypotheses (conjectural status; dissipation and negligible non-gravitational forces) under which the source states it: NARROWED. It is not WRONG, since nothing read refutes the hypothesis or the clumping-entropy link, and the source's own scalings are reproduced (reaudit P3-P4). It is not DATA-DEPENDENT, since the entropy gap stays above 30 dex on any input.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: permute.py:441-443 and 543-545 say 'on Penrose's hypothesis' (a conjectured time-asymmetric law at initial singularities, with no accepted entropy measure) and add 'with dissipation and negligible non-gravitational forces'. Ideally RELAXATION_BELONGS_TO would also be computed, not hardcoded; that affects the scorecard row, not this source comparison. To WRONG: a read counterexample, reproduced here, in which clumping lowers gravitational entropy under the source's p.612 conditions; none was seen. To DATA-DEPENDENT: a datum that closes the >30 dex gap; none can.
